title: Ironhollow Rising Again
premise: Noor Pemberton, a runaway apprentice hiding in the smuggler's warrens of Thornfell, takes in a mute child who speaks in the dead tongue of the Hollow Kings — and discovers the child is a living key to the ancient binding that keeps the winter god Vaskr imprisoned inside the crown of King Aldric. Hunted by the king's witch-finders and courted by rebels who want the binding broken for their own ends, Noor must choose between delivering the child to safety across the mountains or using them to unbind Aldric before Vaskr fully wakes. In the end, Noor breaks the binding at the cost of her own hedge-magic, Aldric dies human and free, and the child — revealed as Vaskr's last innocent fragment — chooses mortality, while Noor stays in Ironhollow to rebuild what survival has cost.
about_author: Kestrel Okafor is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent five years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, and it shows in every treacherous switchback of their prose. They write fantasy about people who survive by knowing the terrain better than the powerful do.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Establishes Noor's life running contraband through Thornfell's hidden roads after fleeing her mentor Maren's strictures on magic. She calculates everything — routes, debts, risks — because calculation kept her alive when trust didn't. Emotional beat: wary self-sufficiency masking loneliness, shattered when she finds a half-frozen child at her door speaking words that make her wards scream.

chapters.title: A Tongue Older Than Stone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The child, whom Noor names Ash, speaks only in the pre-kingdom tongue; when Noor translates fragments using Maren's stolen primer, she realizes the words are binding-liturgy — the language that caged Vaskr. A witch-finder patrol burns a neighboring homestead asking about 'a vessel.' Emotional beat: dread and reluctant protectiveness as Noor understands Ash isn't just hunted, they're a weapon.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. Inside the palace at Ironhollow, Aldric fights for lucidity against Vaskr's growing possession, keeping a secret journal to track which thoughts are his own. He orders his spymaster to find the child whose existence makes the crown 'itch.' Emotional beat: tragic dignity — a good man rationing his remaining self, aware he may already be too far gone.

chapters.title: The Rebel's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Rebel leader Sefa Corvane intercepts Noor on the mountain road, offering safe passage and protection in exchange for delivering Ash to the rebels' loremaster. Noor, exhausted and hunted, nearly accepts — until she sees rebel prisoners branded with the same sigils Maren once warned were hunger-disguised-as-righteousness. Emotional beat: temptation and betrayal of instinct; Noor flees with Ash deeper into the high passes.

chapters.title: Maren's Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor/Ash POV. Starving in an abandoned watch-shrine, Noor finally uses forbidden magic to speak with Ash directly — and the ritual summons an echo of Maren, who reveals the truth: Maren helped bind Vaskr generations ago via a bloodline, and Ash is its last descendant. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into understanding; Noor forgives her mentor and accepts that running was always going to end here.

chapters.title: Witch-Finders at the Ford
chapters.summary: Noor's POV with interludes from witch-finder Captain Ilsette, a true believer who genuinely pities the 'vessels' she burns. Ambushed at the river ford, Noor spends magic she can't afford to drown the pursuit, and Ash speaks their first common-tongue word: 'Don't.' Emotional beat: terror and tenderness colliding — Noor realizes her power is killing her, and Ash knows it.

chapters.title: The Court of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Ash's POV (rendered in strange, liturgical prose). Captured by Sefa's rebels after all, Ash perceives the political machinery around them with eerie clarity: Sefa doesn't want Vaskr freed, she wants to wear him. Meanwhile Aldric's faction secretly contacts Noor through the spymaster, offering alliance. Emotional beat: the child's terrible innocence seeing through every adult's lie.

chapters.title: Two Keys, One Lock
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor bargains with the dying king via smuggler channels: she'll attempt the unbinding if Aldric surrenders the crown willingly — the binding requires consent, which is why Vaskr took it by deception centuries ago. Sefa moves to seize Ash and force the ritual her way. Emotional beat: desperate alliance; love against duty crystallizes as Noor realizes she cares more for Ash and even Aldric than for any cause.

chapters.title: The Unbinding of Aldric
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax in the throne room during the long winter's first full dark. Sefa forces the ritual early; Noor counters using Maren's liturgy and her own life-magic, while Aldric, lucid one final hour, consents to die so Vaskr can be cut loose. Noor burns out her hedge-gift entirely to sever the bond. Emotional beat: sacrificial triumph shadowed by loss — the crown falls empty, and something vast and wounded stands unbound in the snow.

chapters.title: After the Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue-near resolution. The unbound Vaskr confronts Ash — his own severed innocence — and the child offers him mortality: to end as a person rather than rage as a god. Vaskr accepts and fades into the first true spring thaw in memory. Noor, magicless but alive, chooses to stay in Ironhollow raising Ash among people learning to live without kings. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope — survival's price paid, and worth it.
